newsitem.title: FRANCE: France wants more information on gene-maize.
newsitem.headline: France wants more information on gene-maize.

text.p: French farm minister Philippe Vasseur said on Wednesday he needed more scientific data before taking a stance on the controversial issue of imports of genetically-modified maize.
"We lack sufficient elements to draw a firm conclusion," Vasseur told a group of reporters in Paris.
Vasseur said more scientific information was needed because the debate over the safety of gene-altered crops had often led to "excessive" reactions from some parties.
The European Union has already allowed member states to individually import gene modified soybeans but has yet to approve imports of gene-altered maize.
A recent shipment of U.S. soybeans thought to contain gene-altered grain sparked protests from environmentalists and complaints from consumer organisations who fear the crop may be a risk to health.
Three EU scientific and export groups are due to report in December on the safety of approving the sale in the EU of gene-modified maize.
Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has said he will await the findings of the expert groups before making a recommendation.
